title: SP-Aurora: Amazon Aurora provisioned cluster, writer and readers, endpoints, lag, failover and Auto Scaling

sp.name: SP-Aurora
covers: Amazon Aurora (PostgreSQL or MySQL compatible), provisioned: one writer and up to 15 readers, each in an AZ with a promotion tier
Endpoints per connection: cluster (writer), reader (balanced over readers; the writer when there are none), or both (writes to the cluster endpoint, reads to the reader endpoint)
Load per instance: writes only on the writer; reads where the endpoint sends them
Replica lag that grows with the writer's write load, stale-read risk; Global Database lag to region B
Failover: zone or writer loss promotes the reader with the highest priority in a surviving AZ (about 30–60 s), or recreates the writer (about 10 minutes) when there is none
Aurora Auto Scaling of readers: target average reader CPU, minimum and maximum, cooldowns
Terraform: aws_rds_cluster, one aws_rds_cluster_instance per instance (AZ, promotion tier), Application Auto Scaling for readers
not_covered: Custom endpoints, RDS Proxy, write forwarding
Aurora Limitless Database and Aurora DSQL
Per-query simulation over time (the rollup is per instance)

policy.assumptions: lagBaseMs (replica lag with an idle writer) and readerCreateMin (time to add a reader) are NEXUS planning assumptions, not AWS figures: AWS documents lag as usually much less than 100 ms and gives no creation time. Measure AuroraReplicaLag in CloudWatch.

integration.carries: Endpoint (cluster, reader, or both), reads and writes

facts.label: Aurora Replicas (readers) per cluster
facts.note: An Aurora DB cluster can contain up to 15 Aurora Replicas.

facts.label: Reader endpoint
facts.note: Balances each connection request among the Aurora Replicas. With no replicas, it connects to the primary (writer). Balancing is per connection, not per query.

facts.label: Cluster (writer) endpoint
facts.note: Connects to the primary instance; all writes (DML, DDL) go there. After a failover it points to the new primary.

facts.label: Replica lag
facts.note: Usually much less than 100 ms after the primary writes an update; varies with the rate of change and increases during heavy writes.

facts.label: Failover to an Aurora Replica
facts.note: Service is typically restored in less than 60 seconds, and often less than 30 seconds. Reads and writes to the primary fail with an exception during the interruption.

facts.label: No Aurora Replica: the primary is recreated
facts.note: Recreated in the same AZ, typically in less than 10 minutes. If the whole AZ is down and every instance is in it, create a new instance in another AZ yourself.

facts.label: Promotion tier (failover priority)
facts.note: 0 is the highest priority, 15 the lowest. Ties go to the largest instance, then an arbitrary one. Changing it does not trigger a failover.

facts.label: Cluster volume
facts.note: Copies of the data across three Availability Zones in the Region; instances in any AZ read the same volume.

facts.label: Cluster volume maximum size
facts.note: 128 TiB; 256 TiB on specific newer engine versions.

facts.label: Auto Scaling cooldown (scale-out and scale-in)
facts.note: Default 300 s each when not set. Target tracking on average reader CPU or connections; scale-in can be disabled.

facts.label: Auto Scaling in a Global Database secondary
facts.note: Aurora global databases do not support Aurora Auto Scaling for secondary DB clusters.

facts.label: Global Database replication lag
facts.note: Replicates to secondary Regions with latency typically under a second.

facts.label: Global Database secondary Regions
facts.note: Up to 10 read-only secondary Regions; a secondary cluster can have up to 16 read-only instances.

rules.rationale: A reader in another AZ is the failover target: without one, a writer failure means recreating it (about 10 minutes) and an AZ outage needs a new instance created by hand.
rules.fix: Add a reader in another AZ (promotion tier 0 or 1).

rules.rationale: The reader Aurora promotes first should not share the writer's AZ: a zone outage would take both.
rules.fix: Give a reader in another AZ the highest priority.

rules.rationale: Readers serve only connections that use the reader endpoint; through the cluster endpoint every query runs on the writer.
rules.fix: Send read-only connections to the reader endpoint.

rules.rationale: Replica lag grows with the write rate; above about 100 ms, reads through the reader endpoint can miss recent writes.
rules.fix: Read your own writes through the cluster endpoint, or lower the write load on the writer.

rules.rationale: An Aurora cluster has at most 15 Aurora Replicas.
rules.fix: Keep readers (and Auto Scaling maximum) at 15 or fewer.

rules.rationale: Aurora Auto Scaling is not supported for Global Database secondary clusters.
rules.fix: Size the secondary's readers by hand.

rules.rationale: Writes scale only with the writer instance: readers do not take writes.
rules.fix: Scale the writer up, cache reads, or buffer writes in a queue.
